judgment.notes: All phase functions are smooth and have modulus one for real frequencies; their products, differences and derivatives are continuous on the finite interval. Thus the integral estimates and integration by parts have their required regularity. Under L1, alpha and beta are nonzero, so both integration-by-parts divisions are legitimate. BG001-BG003 record the actual routine facts and grounds. There are no E/M applications.

Linearity and the exponential product identity give the stated centered integral for eta. For 0<=s<=tau, the phase difference estimate gives |h(s)|<=(|alpha|/tau) integral_0^tau |s-r| dr<=tau|alpha|, hence the first estimate. At s=0,tau each distance integral equals tau^2/2, giving endpoint sum <=tau|alpha|; also |h'|=|alpha|, so F001 has constant 2*tau|alpha|. Integration by parts then yields 2|alpha|/|beta|=2|alpha/beta|. Symmetry allows the same argument with frequencies interchanged. Taking the smaller bounds gives exactly both requested minima. If alpha*beta=0, a phase is identically one and eta=0. All integrals are of continuous functions on a compact interval; no limit exchange is used.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
